newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BARESI BOWS OUT AFTER 20 YEARS AT MILAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARESI BOWS OUT AFTER 20 YEARS AT MILAN.

text.p: Veteran Italy defender Franco Baresi announced his retirement from professional soccer on Monday after 20 hugely successful consecutive seasons with AC Milan.
Baresi, 37, said he would stay at the club as a vice-president and would also work with the youth team.
"I'm here to confirm that I'm leaving competitive football," he told a packed news conference in Milan. "I've thought about it a lot but I think now's the right moment.
"I'm as moved now as I was when I made my debut. I still can't believe it."
Baresi made his serie A debut with Milan in 1978 and played his last match for the five-times European champions at the end of the 1996-97 season.
When he played his final game at the San Siro earlier this month home fans hung banners around the stadium which read: "Stay with us".
In all, Baresi played 716 official games at the heart of the Milan defence, winning six Italian league titles and three European Cups.
He also played 81 times for his country. Only goalkeeper Dino Zoff (112) and defender Giacinto Facchetti (94) have made more appearances for Italy.
Paolo Maldini, who succeeded Baresi as captain of both Milan and Italy, also has 81, as does midfielder Marco Tardelli.
Born in the northern town of Travagliato on May 8, 1960, Baresi was an orphan by the time he made his serie A debut for Milan on April 23 1978 at the age of 17.
He stayed with the club when they were relegated to serie B for two seasons in the early 1980s and then helped guide them to two European Cups under former Italy coach Arrigo Sacchi in 1989 and 1990.
He captained Milan under Fabio Capello and led them to another European Cup triumph in 1994 and four Italian league titles in the space of five years.
Baresi's international record was equally impressive.
He was a member of the squad which won the 1982 World Cup in Spain and made his international debut in December of that year against Romania.
He was surprisingly omitted from the team which gave a disappointing display at the 1986 World Cup in Mexico but was a virtual fixture in the squad from then on.
He played in the side which finished third on home soil in 1990.
Baresi came back from a knee operation to appear in the 1994 World Cup in the United States and played one of the finest matches of his career in the final against Brazil.
But the match ended in tears as he missed a spot-kick and Italy lost on penalties.
A superb tackler and reader of the game, Baresi also had the ability to push forward out of defence and launch attacks after winning the ball.
